  4. 25-year-old woman, 9 months unable to tolerate intercourse or a speculum tenses and pulls away as the speculum nears T 37.0 °C · BP 114/72 mm Hg · vulva and vestibule normal · swab test painless · microscopy normal · anxious → Involuntary contraction of the pelvic floor muscles → symptoms typically result from levator ani dysfunction: it contracts on attempted penetration; the tissue itself is normal
  5. 38-year-old woman, 4 months of vulvar burning, most of the day with or without sex; intercourse, tampons possible vulva normal: no discharge, redness or skin change cotton swab reproduces the burning pelvic floor relaxed · no yeast · afebrile, menses normal; euthymic → Vulvodynia → vulvar burning most of the day, with or without sex, for at least 3 months with no identifiable cause (normal skin, no yeast); it is not a penetration problem, and 4 months is short of the roughly 6 months GPPPD needs
  6. 24-year-old woman, 4 days of vulvar itching and painful intercourse no pain with sex before this week finished amoxicillin for sinusitis 1 week ago vulva and vagina red, swollen · thick white discharge · T 37.0 °C · calm, euthymic → Vaginal candidiasis → redness, swelling and thick white discharge after antibiotics; microscopy of the discharge confirms, and 4 days is far short of the 6 months GPPPD needs
  7. 35-year-old woman, 8 months without interest in sex no sexual thoughts; never initiates; usually unreceptive little excitement during sex; distressed no pain or fear with penetration Sleeps well; enjoys work, hobbies afebrile, vitals normal · pelvic floor relaxed · euthymic, full affect → Female sexual interest/arousal disorder → at least 3 of the 6 interest and arousal symptoms for 6 months with distress; no pain, and no low mood or anhedonia beyond sex
  8. 58-year-old woman, last menstrual period 7 years ago 1 year of vaginal dryness and burning with intercourse lubricants help only briefly wants to stay sexually active vaginal tissue pale and dry · no discharge · pelvic floor relaxed, nontender · afebrile; euthymic → Low-dose vaginal estrogen → pale, dry postmenopausal tissue: vaginal estrogen is the most effective therapy for symptomatic women
How NBME framed it: question 1

23-year-old woman at a follow-up visit for an oral contraceptive refill sexually active with two male partners; pain has kept her from vaginal intercourse anxious ahead of sexual activity; feels her pelvic floor tighten and block penetration has also been unable to use tampons No history of sexual trauma vital signs normal · speculum hard to advance on pelvic examination

Most likely diagnosis?

Competing answers
  • Generalized anxiety disorder: she is anxious; but that needs 6 months or more of excessive worry about a range of topics with three more symptoms; hers is specific to penetration.
  • Somatic symptom disorder: the complaint is pain; but outside attempted penetration she shows no excessive preoccupation or repeated health-seeking.
  • Vaginal candidiasis: it is associated with vaginismus; but it typically shows vulvar and vaginal redness, swelling and thick white discharge, and the stem gives no antibiotics, diabetes or immunosuppression.
  • Vulvodynia: both hurt at the entrance; but NBME calls it vulvar, not vaginal, pain that is not typically provoked by penetration (the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists also describes provoked, insertional forms); it does not explain a pelvic floor that contracts to prevent penetration.

Down to two: vaginismus or vulvodynia. Vaginismus: pain, anxiety before sex and a pelvic floor that tightens to block penetration, with a speculum that is hard to advance. DSM-5 now calls it genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder; the stem gives no duration and uses the older term.

Transferable rule

When penetration hurts or fails, examine first: inspection looks for a body cause, microscopy tests any discharge, the swab maps vestibular pain and one finger checks the pelvic floor. Difficulty with one or more of penetration, pain, fear of pain or a pelvic floor that tightens, for about 6 months with distress and no body cause, is genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder, treated with pelvic floor therapy and psychotherapy together.

Somatic Symptom and Related Disorders

somatic symptom disorder · illness anxiety · functional neurologic symptoms · factitious disorder · malingeringIs the symptom present, feared, or produced on purpose, and for what reward?

DiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line

Sort by the symptom, then by intent and reward:

  • Somatic symptom disorder: one or more distressing symptoms with excessive thoughts, anxiety or time devoted to them, typically over 6 months
  • Illness anxiety disorder: preoccupation with a serious illness; symptoms absent or mild; at least 6 months
  • Functional neurologic symptom disorder: a motor or sensory symptom incompatible with recognized neurologic disease
  • Factitious disorder: falsified or induced illness, with deception, evident even without an obvious external reward
  • Malingering: deception or overstatement to obtain external incentives

A medical diagnosis does not exclude somatic symptom disorder; the symptoms may or may not be explained.

Treat somatic symptom disorder with regular, time-limited visits rather than symptom-driven ones, and limit further testing.

Diagnosis
Defining criteria Somatic symptom disorder – distressing symptom; disproportionate thoughts, persistent high anxiety, or excessive time and energy; persistent, typically over 6 months · Illness anxiety disorder – preoccupation with having or getting a serious illness; mild or no symptoms; repeated checking or avoidance of care; 6 months or more · Functional neurologic symptom disorder – altered voluntary motor or sensory function; findings incompatible with neurologic disease (eg, Hoover sign)
Sort by symptom, intent and reward
DisorderSymptomsDeception?Motive
Somatic symptom disorderOne or more, distressingNot deceivingExcessive worry about the symptoms
Illness anxiety disorderAbsent or mildFear of disease, not deceptionPreoccupation with a serious illness
Functional neurologic symptom disorderMotor or sensoryIncompatible with neurologic disease–
Factitious disorderFalsified or induced, in self or in another (eg, a child)YesNo obvious external reward
MalingeringFalsified or overstatedYesExternal incentives
Management and treatment
Somatic symptom disorder Visits – regular, time-limited appointments rather than symptom-driven visits · Testing – limit further evaluation; unnecessary tests perpetuate symptom-focused care · Therapy – CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) has the strongest evidence; an SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) or SNRI (serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor) improved symptoms versus placebo · Why it matters – higher disability, health care use, iatrogenic harm and suicidality
Practice
  1. 38-year-old woman with 18 months of back and joint pain six specialists and normal imaging; spends hours a day researching causes has stopped working; sure something serious is missed T 36.7 °C · examination normal · blood count and inflammatory markers normal → Somatic symptom disorder → a distressing symptom with excessive thoughts and time devoted to it, persistent over 6 months; illness anxiety has no or only mild symptoms, and nothing here is feigned for a reward
  2. 29-year-old man sure he has a fatal nerve disease after a friend's diagnosis no weakness; checks his grip strength many times a day worry present for 8 months examination normal · BP 122/78 mm Hg · electromyography normal → Illness anxiety disorder → preoccupation with having a serious illness for at least 6 months with no or mild symptoms and repeated body checking; somatic symptom disorder needs a distressing symptom
  3. 24-year-old woman cannot move her left leg since an argument today pushing down with the left heel when she lifts the right leg against resistance reflexes normal and symmetric · toes downgoing · brain MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) normal · T 36.8 °C → Functional neurologic symptom disorder → weakness incompatible with neurologic disease: the left heel presses down when the right leg lifts (Hoover sign); normal reflexes and MRI argue against a stroke, and nothing suggests deliberate falsification
  4. 33-year-old woman, a pharmacy technician, with a thigh wound that keeps reopening cultures grow different stool organisms each time a syringe found in her bag; no lawsuit or disability claim T 38.2 °C · leukocytes 13,000/mm³ → Factitious disorder → deliberate induction of disease with deception and no obvious external reward; malingering needs an external incentive, and patients with somatic symptom disorder are not trying to deceive
  5. 45-year-old man in police custody asks for oxycodone for back pain pain started at the arrest; limps only when watched court date next week straight-leg raise negative seated and supine · strength and reflexes normal · BP 130/84 mm Hg → Malingering → symptoms overstated to obtain external incentives; factitious disorder deceives without an obvious external reward
  6. 4-year-old boy with a 2nd admission this year for blood in his urine bleeding seen only by his mother; no custody or benefit claim repeated urinalyses normal when nurses collect them T 36.9 °C · BP 96/60 mm Hg · creatinine normal → Factitious disorder imposed on another (mother) → a caregiver falsifies illness in a child without external incentives; the findings exist only in her reports and vanish under observation
  7. 36-year-old woman with abdominal pain for 3 years 11 emergency visits this year, all workups negative; fears a missed cancer asks for another computed tomography scan examination unchanged · BP 118/76 mm Hg · hemoglobin normal → Regular scheduled brief visits → regular, time-limited appointments rather than symptom-driven visits; limit further evaluation, since unnecessary testing can perpetuate symptom-focused health care use; CBT and an SSRI or SNRI can help
Pairs with Panic Disorder and Other Anxiety: is the fear about attacks, or about having a disease?
Transferable rule

Ask two questions before naming it: is the symptom produced on purpose, and is there an external reward?
